name: check3-eval25-ctl
hypothesis: the collapse is unrelated to eval frequency: it reproduces at eval-every 25 (pod pid 1446666, card 3)
result: curve 432/500 (86.4%) at step 25, then 0/500 at 50/75/100; after-arm GSM8K 0/500, MMLU 69.9% (before 75.1%); length trajectory identical to the eval-every-5 control (step 32 mean 336.8, step 33 18.4, step 34 0.0)
finding: eval-every 25 vs 5 changes nothing: rollout trajectory bit-identical to the control run across all 100 steps (40/40 rows diffed steps 1-5, per-step mean lengths match to 0.1, eval-before.jsonl byte-identical). Eval frequency is exonerated as the collapse cause; the collapse is driven by the training trajectory itself.
decision: Stop treating eval frequency as a confound in the collapse attribution. Same-seed same-sha runs stay bit-comparable across trees; the live difference is the sha gap (bd72288 to 2b55eb6, diverging at step 3) plus the advantage-mask absorbing state. Next: A/B before-arm experiment, then decode on/off.

name: eval-incremental-write
cmd: python3 -m tilerl.eval (selftest) + python3 -m tilerl.ledger + uv run pytest + stub-engine timing n=1000
hypothesis: on_row=None overhead is unmeasurable: generate_ids loop wall-clock with the callback path is within 1% of the straight loop on a stub engine (n=1000); a kill mid-eval keeps every row that finished
result: stub engine n=1000, 20 runs: on_row=None 272.2 us/arm, callable 281.5 us/arm, delta 9.2 us (3.4% on the stub), 9 ns per row; selftest + 518 tests green
finding: overhead is bounded above by 9.2 us per arm and unmeasurable on a real arm, where the poll loop is a negligible fraction of wall time; a kill now loses at most the row in flight
decision: incremental write is the default eval path for both arms and every curve point; readers pair on the i key

name: spec-h20-b1
hypothesis: On H20 at B=1, spec depth 1 per-request tok/s exceeds the no-draft baseline; depth 2/3 measured, not assumed (V100 had depth 1 winning 1.25x, H20 width ladder may differ)
result: serving build (fused+graph): d1 0.986x (93.3 vs 94.6 tok/s), d2 0.863x, d3 0.572x; eager build: d1 1.756x, d2 1.824x, d3 1.797x
finding: Spec loses at every depth on the H20 serving build: the W=2 verify costs ~2x the W=1 decode tick and 93.3% acceptance buys only 1.93x tokens. The eager-build win is priced against ~56 ms/tick of host overhead the graph build removes. V100's depth-1 win does not transfer.
decision: Do not enable spec for B=1 serving on H20; the 2026-08-29 entry's pending-remote is flipped to Shipped

name: accspec-b1-repro
hypothesis: On current sha (f80e894) the W=8 spec arm reaches >=130 tok/s and its own base arm lands within +-5% of 78.4 tok/s (74.5-82.3), reproducing the 2026-09-04 1.728x (commit 40bc83c). Falsified if base >82.3 (matches my measured 94.6 serving-build baseline instead) or spec <130.
result: warm re-run, 0 compiles both arms: base 79.5 tok/s (813.4s, 1.00 tok/decode-fwd, 169/200), spec-w8 126.5 tok/s (512.0s, 6.18 tok/decode-fwd, 6.19 of 8 accepted, 168/200). Cold run: 78.2 / 122.4, 26 compiles. Recorded 2026-09-04: 78.4 / 135.5.
finding: Baseline reproduces (78.2/79.5 vs 78.4, within +-5%); spec arm does not (122.4/126.5 vs 135.5). Measured ratio 1.591x, not 1.728x. Drafter acceptance and forward-reduction reproduce (6.18 vs 6.12 tok/fwd, 6.16x fewer forwards); only the spec tick is 7.3% slower. 38/200 completions differ between arms at accuracy within 1 pt. The 78.4-vs-94.6 gap is workload shape (real GSM8K, context past 512 vs 30-tick synthetic), same sha and build.
decision: README headline 135.5/1.728x is exaggerated on the current sha; change it in a separate PR (owner: tilerl-27). Record both decode rows under the bench schema when #350 lands.
